title: PUKY v. SLOVAKIA
summary: In the case of Puky v. Slovakia, the applicant, Mr Ľudovít Puky, is a Slovak national of Romany ethnic origin, represented by the European Roma Rights Centre. The case arose from the vulnerability of Roma communities in Eastern Slovakia, particularly in the context of large-scale police operations following protests by Roma against changes in social welfare policy. On 24 February 2004, after disturbances in Trebišov, police surrounded the Roma settlement, and Mr Puky’s brother, Radoslav, fled the scene, reportedly injured. He was last seen running towards a field, and was later found dead in a drainage ditch, with suffocation by drowning identified as the cause of death. The applicant alleged that the police had physically attacked Roma residents and that the investigation into his brother’s death was inadequate, raising issues under Articles 2 (right to life), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination) of the European Convention on Human Rights. However, the European Court of Human Rights declared the application inadmissible, finding that domestic remedies had not been fully exhausted. This case highlights the persistent challenges Roma and Traveller communities face in seeking accountability and effective protection from state authorities, reflecting broader historical patterns of marginalisation and mistrust in law enforcement across Europe.
